response_text: In order to pass an argument to a thread, the user must define a variable containing the data to be passed. Then, the user passes a pointer to that variable to the os in the osCreateThread() function. Thread functions must be written by the user so that they take a void pointer as an argument, and then cast to the desired data type inside the function. The OS receives the function pointer and a pointer to the data as arguments. When the OS switches to a new thread, it loads the current register values onto the new thread’s stack. The OS must load the data pointer onto R0 so that the data is passed to the function when the new thread begins.\n
